newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close higher on broad-based buying.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close higher on broad-based buying.

text.p: Stocks closed Wednesday higher on broad-based buying and brokers said anticipation of an early expansion of foreign stock ownership limit helped the market remain firm.
The composite stock index rose 6.73 points to 713.67.
A televised briefing by state prosecutors on the Hanbo Steel loan scandal had no impact on the stock market, brokers said.
"Expectation of a raised foreign stock limit boosted the market," said Kim Wan-hee of Dongsuh Securities. "A technical rebound after two days of falls also lifted the market."
The government said it was considering relaxing the foreign stock ownership limit earlier than expected as part of diverse measures to halt the won's depreciation.
South Korea had earlier said it would ease the ceiling to 23 percent for foreign stock investors some time this year from 20 percent at present. But no exact date has been set.
The anticipation boosted some primary blue chips. Samsung Electroncis rose 600 won to 57,500 and KEPCO gained 200 won to 28,000.
In the interim briefing, prosecutors said they had indicted 10 people in connection with the collapse of Hanbo Steel.
Nine of those indicted, including three close aides to President Kim Young-sam, are already in custody. The tenth person to be charged is a former president of Korea First Bank.
"The outcome was widely expected. There were no surprises contained in the prosecutors' announcement," said Kim Duck-sun of Hyundai Securities.

Brokers said active foreign buying of chipmaking shares before the close stimulated LG Semicon and Hyundai Electronics. Both LG and Hyundai went limit up, rising 1,800 won and 2,400 won to 24,800 and 32,400.

Insurance shares were highlighted by the finance and economy ministry draft plan to allow the nation's top five conglomerates to enter the life insurance business this year. The insurance sub-index rose 103.13 points or 2.76 percent to 3,837.01.
Asset-rich shares, pharmaceuticals and shares targetted by mergers and acquisition talks were also in demand.
Sungchang Enterprise rose 1,700 won to 5,450 and Yuhan Corp gained 900 won to 45,900.
Brokers said the market was awaiting President Kim Young-sam's address next week.
